plan.english: Man-Minded, why are you trembling? I am not trembling. I am great. The earth is trembling. The earth is not trembling. A mouse is sitting on your neck. Friend, take it off me! Seize it!

clauses.english: A mouse is sitting on your neck.
clauses.speaker: user

plan.english: Herdsman, your dog lies near the hearth, and the wolf drives off your sheep. My dog and the wolf are friends. They eat them together. Then who guards the sheep? My wife guards them. The wolf is afraid of her.

plan.english: Brother, yesterday I lifted a foal. I lifted a horse. I lifted two horses and a wagon. I lifted the earth. Then where were you standing? I was standing on your neck, brother. Did you not notice?

plan.english: Of-Good-Fame, your horse is swift. Swift is my horse, and swift am I. Yesterday your horse fled from the wolf, and you were sitting on it. I did not flee. I was leading the wolf away from the village. It was following you. It was following me indeed.

plan.english: King, you gave me no reward. Now I will sing against you, and your cattle will die. Sing, guest! They are eating; they do not listen to you. Then I will sing against your wife. Sing! She does not listen to me.

plan.english: Dear guest, are you hungry? I am not hungry. Then why did you eat up my ram? I was thirsty; I was not hungry. Then drink water! I do not drink water. I am a guest.

plan.english: It has dawned, son. Get up! Father, I am thinking. What are you thinking? Who will plough the field? You will plough it! Then I will lie down again.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: Then I will lie down again.

plan.english: Husband, why are you clutching the door? The earth is turning, wife. The earth is not turning. You are drunk. Then why do I see two wives? The two of them are laughing.

plan.english: Elder, tell me: will it rain today? It will rain, boy. How do you know? I know. My wife is drying wool. When she dries wool, it rains.

plan.english: Husband, did you milk the cow? I milked her, Kindly. Then why is her udder swelling? Then what did I milk? You milked the billy goat. He is angry. He is not angry; he is laughing.

plan.english: Mother, tell me a story about the fox. The fox came to the village at night. She saw the sheep. What did she do then? She devoured them. Now lie down. I am afraid of the fox. Do not be afraid. The fox is full.

title: The Mouse That Ate the Feast

plan.english: Husband, who ate up the feast? A mouse ate it up, dear. A mouse devoured a great feast? Then it burst! It did burst. Now it is lying on the bed. You are that mouse!

title: The King's Daughter Who Did Not Laugh

plan.english: A king had a daughter, and she did not laugh. The king said: "If my daughter laughs, I will give her to that man." Many men arrived, and she did not laugh. Then a shepherd's young son came. He was sitting on a billy goat. The goat farted loudly. Then the daughter laughed. The king gave her to the shepherd's son.

clauses.english: A king had a daughter, and she did not laugh.
"If my daughter laughs, I will give her to that man."
Many men arrived, and she did not laugh.
Then a shepherd's young son came.
He was sitting on a billy goat.
The king gave her to the shepherd's son.

plan.english: The fox seized a sparrow. The sparrow said: "Fox, praise the gods, and then eat me!" The fox praised them. And the sparrow fled from her mouth. Then the fox said: "I will not praise them again."

clauses.english: "Fox, praise the gods, and then eat me!"
And the sparrow fled from her mouth.

plan.english: A bear was lying in the field. A mouse climbed over him. The bear woke up and seized the mouse. The mouse trembled. The bear laughed and let it go. The mouse ran to its brothers and said: "Brothers, the bear trembled before me!"

clauses.english: A bear was lying in the field.
The bear woke up and seized the mouse.
The bear laughed and let it go.
The mouse ran to its brothers and said:

plan.english: Two thieves stole a cow by night. It grew light, and the two raged. The old one said: "I stole the cow!" The young one said: "I stole her!" It grew dark. She went to her own home, and the herdsman was milking her.

clauses.english: Two thieves stole a cow by night.
It grew light, and the two raged.
She went to her own home, and the herdsman was milking her.

title: The Man Who Drank the Moon

plan.english: A drunk man saw the moon in the lake. "The moon has sunk into the lake!" he said. "I will drink the lake and free the moon." He drank through the night. It grew light, and the moon vanished. He went home and said: "Wife, I drank the moon." "Now I am full."

clauses.english: A drunk man saw the moon in the lake.
"The moon has sunk into the lake!" he said.
"I will drink the lake and free the moon."
It grew light, and the moon vanished.

plan.english: The fox said to the she-wolf: "When you sing, the sheep tremble." "Go and sing by the village!" The she-wolf went and sang. The shepherds heard her and ran. She ran away. On the other side, the fox seized a ram. Then the fox said: "She-wolf, sing again!" "The ram was tasty."

clauses.english: The fox said to the she-wolf:
The shepherds heard her and ran.
On the other side, the fox seized a ram.

title: The Old Woman and the Thief

plan.english: A thief came by night to an old woman's door. She heard him. She cried aloud: "Husband, stand up!" "Bring the spear!" "Brothers-in-law, come!" The thief ran away. There lived the old woman and a mouse.

clauses.english: A thief came by night to an old woman's door.
There lived the old woman and a mouse.

plan.english: A billy goat was standing on a cart. A bear arrived, and the goat laughed. "Bear, you have no power here!" Then the cart began to turn. It carried the goat toward him. He said: "Come, dear guest!"

clauses.english: A billy goat was standing on a cart.
A bear arrived, and the goat laughed.
Then the cart began to turn.
It carried the goat toward him.

plan.english: At the sacrificial feast an elder was praising Perkʷunos. Then he farted loudly. The young men laughed. The elder said: "Do not laugh!" "Perkʷunos rumbled." "He heard me." Then the young men praised Perkʷunos.

clauses.english: At the sacrificial feast an elder was praising Perkʷunos.
Then the young men praised Perkʷunos.

title: Riddle of the Roaring in the House

plan.english: At night someone roars beside my hearth. Is that Perkʷunos? It does not rain. It is my husband, lying on the bed.

clauses.english: At night someone roars beside my hearth.
It is my husband, lying on the bed.

plan.english: It eats, and it does no work. It is not my brother-in-law. If it drinks water, it dies. My brother-in-law does not drink water. It is fire.

clauses.english: It eats, and it does no work.
If it drinks water, it dies.
My brother-in-law does not drink water.

plan.english: No one brings him, and he comes to the feast. He eats in front of the king. The heroes tremble before him, and the women cry aloud. He is the mouse.

clauses.english: No one brings him, and he comes to the feast.
He eats in front of the king.
The heroes tremble before him, and the women cry aloud.

plan.english: Who sees two moons in the sky? Who talks to a stake? Who lies in front of the door, and his wife climbs over him? The drunk man.

clauses.english: Who sees two moons in the sky?
Who lies in front of the door, and his wife climbs over him?

title: Riddle of the Old Man's Voice

plan.english: I am born from an old man. I have no mouth, and I speak. The guests hear me and go away. No one praises me. The old man has farted.

clauses.english: I am born from an old man.
I have no mouth, and I speak.
The guests hear me and go away.

plan.english: The thief fears her; her husband fears her. When she sees a mouse, she cries aloud and climbs onto the cart. Who is she? She is the wife.

clauses.english: The thief fears her; her husband fears her.
When she sees a mouse, she cries aloud and climbs onto the cart.

title: Praise of Man-Minded, Slayer of the Mouse

plan.english: Man-Minded, great is your fame. You did slay the swift mouse beside the hearth. Then the mouse was lying down, and you indeed were trembling. Three times you struck it with the spear, Man-Minded. Hero, your fame is imperishable. Your brother and sister are laughing.

clauses.english: You did slay the swift mouse beside the hearth.
Then the mouse was lying down, and you indeed were trembling.
Three times you struck it with the spear, Man-Minded.
Your brother and sister are laughing.

plan.english: Guest, you who devour the rams, and you who drink our dregs, you who lie on our bed, hear us! Go over there; may the gods give you good things over there.

clauses.english: Guest, you who devour the rams,
and you who drink our dregs,
you who lie on our bed, hear us!
Go over there; may the gods give you good things over there.

plan.english: Now let us sing of the drunken man. He drank the lake, and he drank the river. Then at dawn he thirsts again. And he sings in front of the door. Now may he live, and may the dregs not be gone from him!

clauses.english: Now let us sing of the drunken man.
He drank the lake, and he drank the river.
Then at dawn he thirsts again.
And he sings in front of the door.
Now may he live, and may the dregs not be gone from him!

plan.english: Mice, brothers, cry aloud! The old guest has come to our home. He ate up the feast and licked the hearth. And now there is nothing for us. We are hungry; let us flee to the field!

clauses.english: The old guest has come to our home.
He ate up the feast and licked the hearth.
And now there is nothing for us.
We are hungry; let us flee to the field!

plan.english: Now let me sing of my son, the hero. In the field he ploughs nothing. He lifts nothing, and he carries nothing. At the feast he eats the ram, and he drinks. Now may his fame be great!

clauses.english: Now let me sing of my son, the hero.
In the field he ploughs nothing.
He lifts nothing, and he carries nothing.
At the feast he eats the ram, and he drinks.
Now may his fame be great!
